answer: Each agent mints a unique cryptographic token stamped with a pigment‑derived hash of its hardware fingerprint; when an agent invites a new node, the invite token echoes the inviter’s hash and the network records a lotus‑shaped Merkle proof linking them. The protocol only distributes referral rewards after verifying that the new token’s fingerprint differs by a minimum entropy threshold, otherwise the reward is zero. An attacker must forge distinct hardware hashes and assemble valid Merkle paths, raising the cost to thousands of physical devices and prohibitive compute.
